To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the top-down estimate of Chinese NOx emissions in July 2009 is about 6.8 (5.7) TgN/ yr for China (East China), and that the top-down emissions exceed the a prior i by 20-40% (10-30%) over most of China (East China).
the top-down emissions of NO x from the four anthropogenic sectors are constrained by combining the GOME-2/OMI retrievals, and the top-down emissions for East China in 2006 are 6.8 (5.5) TgN/ yr.

anthropogenic emissions in China are 6.8 (5.5) TgN/ yr, 17 (10)% lower than the bottom-up estimates, and the a posteriori emissions in East China are 5.7 (4.6) TgN yr-1, 16 (14)% lower than the a-priori bottom-up estimates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new methodology to constrain Chinese anthropogenically emitted NOx from different sectors.

the following: a) a new approach to top-down estimation of NO x emissions in East China; b) a new constraint on anthropogenic emissions from different sectors; and c) a new estimate of the national NO x budget in China.
a new methodology to improve satellite-based top-down constraints of NOx emissions, and a new estimate of NOx emissions in China.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the top-down estimate is 6.8±2.1 (1 σ) TgN/ yr (5.5±1.7 Tg/yr for East), and the a priori estimate is 6-7 TgN (4-5 TgN for East).
the a priori emission inventory from INTEX-B for 2006 is likely to be within a factor of 2 of the actual emission in July 2007.

our best top-down estimate for national emissions in 2008 is 6.8±0.9 TgN/ yr (5.5±0.7 Tg N/yr for East), with the error bars representing the combined effects of systematic errors of satellite retrievals and other factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the top-down estimate is robust against most factors and is likely to have a systematic error of no more than 15% (10% for East China).
the anthropogenic emissions of NOx in China have been constrained by our top-down analysis to a level comparable to the a priore bottom-up estimates.
the anthropogenic emissions in China are likely in the range of 5.7-6.8 Tgyr, which is significantly higher than the inventory-based estimate of 4.8 Tg/yr for the same year.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new methodology can provide useful constraints on NOx emissions in China, and that the top-down emissions can be used to improve the a priori estimates for bottom-up emission inventories.
the top-down estimate of NOx emissions in China is not very sensitive to individual uncertainties, which is encouraging.
the satellite-based approach can be a powerful and useful tool for constraining emissions of NOx in China, and it can be applied to other regions and other species in the future.
